_marker: THE HARD CORPUS — cases this repo AUTHORS in order to be converted, each aimed at ONE mechanism a closed table already names, each declaring its expected outcome BEFORE the conversion runs. A corpus we author is reproducible by construction, which is the whole reason it exists: it kills the "not re-derivable from its own inputs" class outright. Hand-authored; the DENOMINATORS below are re-derived from their own tables by `npm run hard-corpus:check` and a table that moves fails the gate. Sorted by id, byte-stable.

rootCauses.file: this file — the ONE hand-entered denominator
rootCauses.note: RC1-RC8 are the burn-down triage classes; they live in no repo file, so they are transcribed here and the gate checks cases against THIS list rather than re-deriving them

rootCauses.title: layout-axis-door — the only reader that turns a captured flex keyword into a Part.layout fact is narrower than the schema it writes into and narrower than both emitters, so a composite mints as one row
declared-uniform-only — the declared/keyword-channel door carries UNIFORM values only, so an axis-varying keyword drops and the variant plane mints byte-identical cells
nonstroke-ink-no-lowering — ink the CSS paints by a non-fill/non-stroke mechanism (outline pair, box-shadow ring, elevation) has no canvas lowering, so rings, borders and surfaces vanish
glyph-reconstruction — SVG reconstruction drops the channels that carry the glyph STATE and SHAPE
empty-slot-hugs-to-1px — a childless native SLOT hugs to 1px, so every slot-bearing component mints as a sliver or an empty box
stale-token-alias — a re-anchored token alias is never re-verified at MINT time, so a drifted DS token silently repaints the component
placeholder-empty-and-value-ink — a leaf form control mints an EMPTY placeholder string in VALUE ink, so every empty field reads as filled (or as nothing)
geometry-excluded-for-text-parts — width/height are excluded from fusion for every text-bearing part, so a sized component hugs its sample string

cases.why: RC1. baseline is already in LayoutSchema.align and already lowered by both emitters; only the DETECTION map lacked it, so the fact could never arrive from a captured library. spec/channel-table.json classes align-items CARRIED (counterAxisAlignItems).

RC3, ledger half. A dashed border is real ink with no Figma stroke-style spelling. spec/channel-table.json classes border-top-style LEDGERED: it rides Part.declared and surfaces as a code-only fact, so it must reach the CONTRACT and must NOT be drawn.

RC3. The single-shadow case is covered; the ELEVATION shape real design systems ship is a stack, and the emitter carried a narrower literal-colour parser than the token set does. spec/channel-table.json classes box-shadow CARRIED (DROP_SHADOW single, or the full multi-layer/inset effect stack, v17).

RC5. A childless slot hugs to 1px, so every slot-bearing component mints as a sliver or an empty box. The CSS-side precondition is that a region with NO children and no fixed size still reaches the contract carrying its minimum box. spec/channel-table.json classes min-height and min-width CARRIED (minHeight / minWidth).

RC1. LAYOUT_CHANNEL_TO_FIELD is the only reader that turns a captured flex keyword into a Part.layout fact, and the reversed spellings were absent from it: no map entry means the channel leaves through layout-value-outside-vocabulary and the composite mints as one row. spec/channel-table.json classes flex-direction CARRIED (auto-layout layoutMode).

RC1. LayoutSchema.wrap is a first-class contract fact with a lowering on both surfaces, but spec/channel-table.json classes flex-wrap REFUSED (code-only:no-schema-channel): wrapping flex containers are outside the single-line auto-layout lowering. The case measures whether the refusal is NAMED rather than silent.

RC3, third mechanism. The pseudo-gradient case is REFUSED; a gradient on the element itself is the surface every hero card and every gradient button paints with. spec/channel-table.json classes background-image CARRIED (gradient stacks mint as a whole-value gradient kind).

RC3. Ink the CSS paints by a non-fill/non-stroke mechanism has no canvas lowering unless the outline PAIR (width + colour) both survive; the existing antd cases only exercise the focus-visible plane. spec/channel-table.json classes outline-width and outline-color CARRIED as an OUTSIDE-aligned stroke pair, outline-offset LEDGERED (annotate).

RC7. The emitter mints an empty placeholder string in VALUE ink, so every empty field reads as filled. This case measures the INPUT to that defect: the control element carries its value ink and nothing else, because the ::placeholder plane is a separately named wall (see the pseudo-placeholder case). spec/channel-table.json classes color CARRIED (the text node fill).

RC4. The other half of glyph geometry: a check mark that is not SVG at all but a rotated two-border box. pseudo-decor v2 promotes a drawn pseudo into a part; spec/channel-table.json classes border-right-width CARRIED (strokeRightWeight) and transform CARRIED for the bounded rotate() grammar.

The em case is covered and rem is not: em resolves against the element, rem against the document root, and a capture harness owns the document root. spec/channel-table.json classes padding-left CARRIED (paddingLeft); the case measures that the resolved px reaches the contract rather than the authored rem.

RC4. SVG reconstruction drops the channels that carry the glyph SHAPE: a check mark drawn as a stroked path is the single most common indicator in every checkbox in every design system. spec/channel-table.json classes stroke-width and stroke CARRIED (verbatim in the promoted glyph markup) and stroke-linecap REFUSED.

RC8, adjacent class. The accessible-name-only pattern: real text that paints nowhere near its box. spec/channel-table.json classes text-indent LEDGERED (a contract token binding emitted verbatim in generated CSS; on canvas an annotation only), so it must reach the CONTRACT and must NOT move the text on canvas.

RC8. width/height are excluded from fusion for every text-bearing part on the premise that text widths are font-metric-dependent — a premise that is false for a box the layout PINNED. spec/channel-table.json classes width and height CARRIED (a fixed frame size).

notCovered.why: DESIGNED, NOT BUILT this round. Hand-built Figma sets on the scratch file page `hard corpus 2026-08-25` targeting nested auto-layout with mixed hug/fill, absolute-positioned children, component properties (boolean/text/instance-swap), many-axis variant sets, variable modes, text styles, detached instances and overlay-shaped sets. The design is in spec/HARD-CORPUS.md; no set exists yet, and no case in this manifest declares direction canvasToCode.

notCovered.mechanism: the complex archetypes — calendar, data table, combobox
notCovered.why: DESIGNED, NOT BUILT this round. These are the archetypes the owner explicitly fears and they are exactly where the required-facts table has the least evidence; each needs a multi-part authored component and a prop space, which the conformance fixture cannot express (see the next row).

NOT REACHABLE from the conformance fixture as it stands: conformance/build.ts writes an EMPTY prop space per case ("the fixture varies CSS, not props"), so no case can carry two enum axes. RC2 and half of RC3/RC4 are products over axes and cannot be measured until the fixture grammar grows an axis. Named here rather than half-built.
NO CASE. RC2 needs a variant axis (see above). RC6 lives in the computed-capture DECISION LEDGER, which only exists for a library that has one — an authored case has no decisions.json to drift.

notCovered.mechanism: the emitter halves of RC5 and RC7
notCovered.why: NOT REACHABLE from a CSS/DOM fixture. The slot birth box and the placeholder-ink fallback both live in core/emit-figma-script.ts and are driven by CONTRACT constructs (slots, placeholder-color) that no capture produces. They need an authored CONTRACT case on the emit lane (bundle to mock canvas to dump to propose), which conformance/canvas.ts already provides the chain for. Designed, not built.
DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, not an omission: an INERT row has provably no independent visual effect at computed level, so there is no outcome for a case to expect.
